subject: Clarify IP indemnity scope and evidence ownership for EdgeWave order form
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify IP indemnity scope and evidence ownership for EdgeWave order form

Kimberly / Priyom — attaching my latest order form redlines. EdgeWave pushed back hard on the defend-or-reimburse split for third-party infringement; they want defend in all cases unless we can show direct model training misuse. My ask: can legal confirm (1) whether we can accept a narrower defend obligation limited to "model-output claims" and (2) who on our side will own evidence collection if we accept the narrowed language?

Notes:
- EdgeWave flagged their procurement team needs a clear evidence owner for any notice (they want technical logs + prompt history).
- We currently store customer prompts in ephemeral KV cache for <24 hours on hosted; Dedicated and Private have different retention.

Attachments: EdgeWave_OrderForm_redlines_v2.pdf (redlines), evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx (draft mapping)

Next step: Kimberly — recommend legal position. Priyom — please confirm where engineering can export prompt/response traces and SLA for evidence retrieval.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify IP indemnity scope and evidence ownership for EdgeWave order form

Ben — thanks. High level response before I read the redlines in detail:

1) Defend vs reimburse: We should aim to accept a defend obligation for third-party claims only where the claim relates to (a) outputs produced by the model as served to the customer under the order form, and (b) a third party alleges direct infringement by the output itself (not underlying model weights or training data). This is narrower than a blanket defend.

2) Evidence & notice: We can accept an evidence owner mapping but cannot commit to retention that violates privacy/customer-specified retention on Private deployments. We should propose: Redwood provides a standard evidence bundle (service logs, request IDs, timestamped model version, and KV cache trace if available) within the SLA window; customer is responsible for preserving any additional context outside our retention window.

3) Operational owner: Legal needs an internal triage owner for all notices. I suggest Priyom's team (Product Ops) be the technical evidence lead; CS (assigned later) will own customer communications. Priyom — confirm feasibility and timelines for a 72-hour evidence pull for Dedicated and 7 days for Hosted (default).

I'll open a redline pass on the MSA/Order Form: we should add an explicit carveout for upstream model-provider claims and exclude claims tied to customer's post-processing or customer-supplied prompts that induce infringement (narrow carveout language attached).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Moran <alice.moran@edgewave.io>

Cc: EdgeWave Legal <legal@edgewave.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify IP indemnity scope and evidence ownership for EdgeWave order form

Ben — thanks for the redlines. A few things from EdgeWave side:

- We cannot accept a carveout that shifts the burden to us for "customer-supplied prompts" without clear guidance — some of our product flows generate prompts programmatically.
- We need Redwood to guarantee availability of request & response traces for at least 90 days for Dedicated customers; otherwise compliance won't sign off.
- Regarding model-provider claims: we need defensibility for outputs produced by the specific model version we run under the order form. If there's a vulnerability in upstream weights, we still expect Redwood to defend for outputs served during our contract window.

Can Kimberly propose redline language that preserves defensibility while giving us assurance on evidence access? Also, can you confirm whether any of the requested evidence would include raw customer content (we have strict internal policies).

Best,
Alice Moran
Head of Procurement | EdgeWave

Quick operational note:

- Evidence availability: For Dedicated deployments we can provide a 90-day export of request/response logs and model version metadata if the customer enables "audit retention" at signup (this increases storage cost). Hosted customers default to 30 days retention for request/response bodies; we can do 72-hour full KV cache dump. Private (on-prem) is governed by customer infra.
- Timeline: we can deliver a packaged evidence export within 72 hours for Dedicated if retention is enabled; 7 days for Hosted where data is still present. We cannot guarantee retrieval beyond configured retention windows.

I'll update the evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx to show the mapping: Redwood (technical export), CS (customer preservation liaison), Legal (triage + redline). Will attach updated matrix in next email.

Priyom Das
Product Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moran <alice.moran@edgewave.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 19:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify IP indemnity scope and evidence ownership for EdgeWave order form

Alice / Ben — thanks for the quick replies. Proposed compromise below (I'll insert exact language into the attached redline PDF):

1) Defendant scope: Redwood will defend/reimburse third-party claims that the customer's use of the service, as configured and served under the Order Form, infringes a third party's IP, limited to direct infringement by model output. Excluded: claims arising from (a) customer's modification of output, (b) customer's own training data or models, or (c) pre-existing third-party claims against upstream model providers where the claim does not relate to the specific output actually delivered to the customer.

2) Evidence access and retention: For Dedicated customers, Redwood will provide a standard evidence bundle (request IDs, timestamps, model version, and request/response traces) for up to 90 days where the customer has enabled audit retention; for Hosted customers, default retention is 30 days, with an option to purchase extended retention. Redwood will not disclose customer content beyond what is necessary for legal defense and will work with the customer to redact PII or content-sensitive fields where required.

3) Operational owners and SLA: Priyom's team will be the technical evidence owner (evidence extraction and packaging). Customer Success will be responsible for customer-side preservation instructions and any long-term evidence custody. Legal will triage notices and engage external counsel if needed. Redwood proposes a 72-hour turnaround for initial evidence package production for Dedicated (subject to retention config) and a best-effort 7-day window for Hosted.

4) Dispute mechanism: If parties disagree about whether a claim falls inside the carveout, the parties will use an expedited meet-and-confer; during the meet-and-confer, Redwood will preserve collected evidence.

Alice — can you confirm that this compromise is workable for EdgeWave procurement? If yes, Ben, please send an updated Order Form redline to procurement and upload the evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx to the deal record.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
